title: Instrument Mixer
line1: Sets this slot's audio level, route, and pan.
line2: Mixer settings affect synth and sampler audio, not external MIDI notes.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Mixer > Route
title: Route
line1: direct sends this instrument straight to the main mix; fxb1, fxb2, fxb3 or fxb4 sends it through that FX bus.
line2: MIDI instruments go out as MIDI and skip the internal effects.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Mixer > Pan Pos
title: Pan Position
line1: Sets direct-output pan for this slot's audio.
line2: 0 is left, 16 center, 32 right; bus-routed audio uses the bus pan.

title: FX Buses
line1: Configures shared audio buses used by instrument routes.
line2: Each bus runs Slot 1, Slot 2, then Slot 3, pans the result, and joins the main mix.

title: Bus Names
line1: Sets auto-naming and custom name for each bus.
line2: Auto name is computed from the assigned FX slot types; turning off auto lets you edit the name freely.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > Names > Bus *
title: Bus Name
line1: Configures naming for this bus.
line2: Auto Label on derives a label from FX slot types; Name lets you type any text when Auto is off.

title: FX Bus
line1: Builds one shared bus chain for any instruments routed to this bus.
line2: Slot 1 feeds Slot 2 feeds Slot 3, then Volume and Pan Pos place the bus in the stereo main mix.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Volume
title: FX Bus Volume
line1: Sets the bus output level from 0 to 100 after the FX chain.
line2: Use it to balance everything routed through this bus.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Pan Pos
title: FX Bus Pan Position
line1: Sets where this bus output sits in the stereo mix.
line2: 0 is left, 16 center, 32 right.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Slot 1

title: Global FX
line1: Processes the full stereo main mix after instruments and FX buses are summed together.
line2: These slots run before momentary Play FX and Master Vol, so they color the whole output.

title: Global FX Slot
line1: Configures one stereo master effect slot.
line2: Choose Type, then edit the parameters shown below.

path: Menu > Shape > Global FX > Slot * > Type
title: Slot Type
line1: none=passthrough; vinyl=lo-fi warp/crackle; eq=three-band tone shaping.
line2: compressor=stereo dynamics; saturator=soft clipping; distortion=harder clipping. Selecting an effect initializes its defaults.

path: Menu > Shape > Global FX > Slot * > vinyl
title: vinyl
line1: Lo-fi stereo master effect with warm saturation, crackle, and shared warp movement.
line2: Designed as a lighter-weight master color effect for current Pi Zero targets.

path: Menu > Shape > Global FX > Slot * > compressor
title: compressor
line1: Stereo-linked dynamics processor for the summed main mix.
line2: Threshold, ratio, attack, release, makeup gain, and dry/wet mix affect both channels together.

path: Menu > Shape > Global FX > Slot * > eq
title: eq
line1: Stereo three-band equalizer for the summed main mix.
line2: Use it for broad tonal shaping after instrument and bus routing.

path: Menu > Shape > Global FX > Slot * > saturator
title: saturator
line1: Soft-clipping saturation applied to the stereo main mix.
line2: Useful for gentle density and warmth without adding extra routing.

path: Menu > Shape > Global FX > Slot * > distortion
title: distortion
line1: Harder clipping/shaping applied to the stereo main mix.
line2: Use sparingly; aggressive settings can dominate the full output.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Mixer > Volume
title: Mixer Volume
line1: Sets the per-instrument post-voice fader from 0 to 100.
line2: The Play mix page also controls this value from the grid.

title: Play
line1: Performance grid layer for live mix, pan, route, tempo, LFO, Faders, FX, X/Y, transpose, rate, and Trigger Gate pages.
line2: Fn + left column selects a layer; Fn + right column a technical page, Shift+Fn + right column a musical page.

title: Mix Page
line1: Live grid page: the bottom row mutes each instrument, live only and never saved; the rows above set its volume.
line2: Hold Shift for buses B1-B4 (volume, live mute) and the master volume in the sixth column.

title: Pan Page
line1: Live grid page: one row per instrument, hard left to hard right.
line2: Instruments routed to an FX bus move that bus's pan instead.

title: Route Page
line1: Live grid page per instrument: rows 0-4 route direct or to B1-B4, row 5 bypasses B1-B4 and Global FX 1-2, row 7 sets every bus duck's Source.
line2: Routes and duck sources are saved. Bypass is live only and resets on load; press the same tile again to undo.

title: Tempo Page
line1: Live grid page: tempo tiles 50-240, nudges, Tap, and the Swing A and B rows.
line2: Under external sync, tempo, nudge and Tap are locked to the incoming clock; Swing still works.

title: LFO
line1: One row per LFO, LFO1 at the bottom: column 0 switches it, columns 1-7 pick its period.
line2: Press a lit period again for its triplet; Shift + columns 1-7 set Depth.

title: Faders Page
line1: Live grid page: eight vertical sliders, one per column; a press sets that column's target, Shift + press its second one.
line2: A press writes the value like a menu edit; each bar shows its target's current value, so menu edits and preset loads move it too.

title: Fader Column
line1: One grid column: a plain press sets Target, Shift + press sets S+Target.
line2: A side without a target ignores presses and stays dark.

title: Fader Target
line1: Chooses the parameter a plain press sets; the bottom row gives Range Min, the top row Range Max.
line2: A new target changes nothing until the next press.

title: Fader Shift Target
line1: Chooses the parameter Shift + press sets, with its own range and invert.
line2: A new target changes nothing until the next press.

title: Fader Target
line1: Browses the parameters a Faders slider can set.
line2: Pick one to bind it; (none) clears the slider.

title: Fader Invert
line1: When On, the top row gives the bottom of the range and the bottom row the top.
line2: Needs a Target; it applies from the next press.

title: Fader Shift Invert
line1: Flips the Shift slider: the top row gives the bottom of the range.
line2: Needs an S+Target; it applies from the next press.

title: Action Cols
line1: Turns this many columns, counted from the right, from sliders into action and parameter tiles, 0 to 8.
line2: Tile mappings are saved with the patch and stay put when you shrink the count, so they come back when you grow it again.

title: Tile Map
line1: Sets up one action-column tile: pick its type and what it does, then Map to Grid.
line2: Action tiles run an Aux click action, Shift + press their second one; param tiles step a parameter up, Shift + press down.

path: Menu > Play > Faders > Tile Map > Type
title: Tile Type
line1: none clears a tile; action runs an action; param steps a parameter by one menu step per press.
line2: The rows below follow the type. Mapping none onto a tile clears it.

title: Tile Action
line1: Picks the action a plain press runs; S+Action picks the one Shift + press runs.
line2: Same actions as an Aux click. A behavior action runs on the layer it was picked on; if that layer's behavior lacks it, it shows not active.

title: Set Tile Action
line1: Picks this action for the Tile Map; Map to Grid then stores it on a tile.
line2: (none) leaves that side of the tile without an action.

path: Menu > Play > Faders > Tile Map > Target: *
title: Tile Parameter
line1: Picks the parameter a param tile steps: a press goes one menu step up, Shift + press one step down, like an Aux detent.
line2: The step goes through the menu row, so it saves and autosaves like a menu edit.

path: Menu > Play > Faders > Tile Map > Target: * > *
title: Tile Parameter
line1: Browses the parameters a param tile can step.
line2: Pick one to use it for the next Map to Grid.

path: Menu > Play > Faders > Tile Map > Map to Grid
title: Map to Grid
line1: Waits for a press on an action-column tile and stores the Tile Map there.
line2: Back leaves without changes; with type none the press clears that tile. Needs Action Cols above 0.

title: FX Page
line1: Configures and performs momentary Play FX: hold a mapped tile to run its effect.
line2: It sits in the Shift+Fn bank: Shift+Fn + the bottom right tile opens it.

title: Trigger Gate Page
line1: Live grid page: one row per layer (L1 bottom) picks 0%, custom or 100%; the bottom row's right three tiles set every layer.
line2: Shift+Fn + left column switches a layer off and back; held notes release and do not come back on re-enable.

title: Transpose Page
line1: Live grid page: shifts Synth, FM, Plucked and MIDI notes, and Sampler/Drum ones with Follow Transp. on.
line2: Left column selects layers, Shift + left column all of them; piano tiles choose semitone offsets.

title: Rate Page
line1: Live grid page: one row per layer (L1 bottom) sets its Build Step Rate from 1/32 to 1/2; hold Shift for its Link Scan Unit.
line2: Straight green (Scan Unit white), triplet blue; the new value starts on the next step. Pressing the lit tile resyncs that layer to the next bar.

title: XY Page
line1: Live grid page for X/Y parameter modulation.
line2: Shift + press latches the position past release, even with center release; a plain press clears it.

title: Aux Map
line1: Shows the Play FX parameters and actions that are auto-mapped to aux controls.
line2: Rows wear the same Aux caps as the live auto-mapped controls; values can be edited here, but mappings are not changed.

title: BPM
line1: Sets master tempo, 40-240 BPM.
line2: This is the main tempo control; Play Tempo sets it from the grid.

title: Swing A
line1: Swing is the ratio A:B of each beat's on-beat eighth to its offbeat eighth.
line2: Equal values (4:4) are straight; 5:3 delays the offbeat, 3:5 pulls it early. A change waits for the next beat. MIDI clock out stays straight.

title: Swing B
line1: Sets B, the offbeat eighth's share of the A:B swing ratio (1-7).
line2: Equal to Swing A is straight; higher than A pulls the offbeat earlier.

title: FX Type
line1: The effect a mapped tile plays while held: none, stutter, freeze, filter sweep, pitch, tape stop,
line2: reverse, gate, dub (echo throw), wash, HP riser or crush; changing it loads that effect's defaults.

title: Rate
line1: Sets the captured segment repeat rate (1-32 Hz). Higher rate = shorter captured segment.
line2: Stored per grid tile when Map to Grid is used.

title: Depth
line1: How much stutter or gate you hear, from 0 (dry) to 100 (full).
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Release
line1: Sets the release fade time: freeze fades its capture (10-5000 ms), wash fades its reverb tail (100-8000 ms).
line2: It controls how quickly the effect fades after releasing its grid tile; Map to Grid stores it per tile.

title: Mix
line1: How much of the effect you hear, from 0 (dry) to 100 (all effect).
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Cutoff
line1: Where the filter sweep ends: filter sweep darkens toward it, HP riser thins toward it.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Res
line1: How much the swept filter rings, 0 to 100.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Sweep In
line1: How long the filter takes to reach Cutoff after you press the tile.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Sweep Out
line1: How long the filter takes to open again after you let go.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Semitones
line1: How far pitch shifts, up to two octaves either way.
line2: Cents adds fine tuning on top.

title: Cents
line1: Fine tuning on top of Semitones, up to a semitone either way.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Slide In
line1: Sets pitch glide-in time (10-3000 ms) with linear octave motion. Wet activation still uses a fixed 10 ms anti-click ramp.
line2: Stored per grid tile when Map to Grid is used.

title: Slide Out
line1: How long the pitch takes to glide back after you let go.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Stop
line1: How long the tape takes to grind to a halt while you hold the tile.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Start
line1: How long the tape takes to spin back up after you let go.
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Length
line1: Sets the reverse window (50-1000 ms). Reverse listens for one Length, then plays each latest Length backwards.
line2: Stored per grid tile when Map to Grid is used.

title: Rate
line1: How fast the gate chops, as a note value from 1/32T to 1/4.
line2: It follows the tempo, or the incoming clock.

title: Smooth
line1: How soft the gate's edges are, from 0 (hard) to 100 (round swells).
line2: Each tile keeps the value it was mapped with.

title: Time
line1: The echo time of the dub throw, as a note value from 1/16T to 1/2.
line2: It follows the tempo like Rate.

title: Feedback
line1: How much of each echo comes back, 0 to 90.
line2: The echoes keep trailing off after you let go.

title: Size
line1: Sets the wash reverb size from 0 (short tail) to 100 (long swell).
line2: Stored per grid tile when Map to Grid is used.

title: Bits
line1: Sets the crush bit depth (1-16). Fewer bits sound grittier.
line2: Stored per grid tile when Map to Grid is used.

title: Downsample
line1: Sets the crush sample-rate divider (1-32). Higher values hold each sample longer for aliasing crunch.
line2: Stored per grid tile when Map to Grid is used.

title: Behavior
line1: Picks the little world this layer runs.
line2: Choose a category, then a behavior. Only this layer changes.

title: Layer Behavior
line1: Opens the behavior browser for this layer.
line2: Choose a category, then choose a behavior. Selection updates that layer's Build rows without switching the active layer.

title: Human Behaviors
line1: Playable and manually-steered layer behaviors.
line2: Use these for direct input, looping, sequencing, and hand-shaped world-bubbles.

title: Rhythm Behaviors
line1: Pattern engines for pulses, breaks, fills, and grooves.
line2: These worlds focus on timing structure before pitch or cellular motion.

title: Musical Behaviors
line1: Melodic and harmonic phrase engines.
line2: Use these for motifs, chords, canons, contours, and longer musical arcs.

title: Cellular Behaviors
line1: Classic grid automata and neighborhood systems.
line2: Small cell rules can become surprisingly lively musical motion.

title: Field Behaviors
line1: Continuous fields, waves, drops, and reaction systems.
line2: These worlds smear energy across the grid instead of stepping tile by tile.

title: Geometry Behaviors
line1: Shape, maze, and fractal pattern builders.
line2: Good for spatial structure and crisp visual-musical forms.

title: Growth Behaviors
line1: Organic spreading, branching, and accretion systems.
line2: Use these when you want the grid to feel like it is growing something.

title: Motion Behaviors
line1: Moving particles, orbits, gravity, and flowing systems.
line2: These worlds put travel and momentum at the center of the pattern.

title: Behavior
line1: The behavior this layer runs: none, life or brain.
line2: none is an empty layer; life is Conway's Life; brain fires, rests and recovers.

title: Step Rate
line1: How fast this layer's world moves: one step per 1/32T, 1/32, 1/16T, 1/16, 1/8T, 1/8,
line2: 1/4T, 1/4, 1/2T, 1/2, 1/1T or 1/1 (T means triplet). A scanning layer plays at its Scan Unit.

title: Step Rate
line1: How fast this layer's world moves: one step per 1/32T, 1/32, 1/16T, 1/16, 1/8T, 1/8,
line2: 1/4T, 1/4, 1/2T, 1/2, 1/1T or 1/1 (T means triplet). A scanning layer plays at its Scan Unit.

title: Spawn Count
line1: Sets how many new cells, agents or other entities this behavior's spawn action adds.
line2: Higher values make spawn actions denser and more disruptive.

title: Spawn Interval
line1: Sets the tick interval between automatic random spawn bursts.
line2: Lower values spawn more frequently.

title: Reset
line1: Starts this layer's world over.
line2: Its settings stay as they are.

title: Select Behavior
line1: Runs this behavior on the layer.
line2: It switches right away.

title: None
line1: Keeps the layer's grid empty and ignores grid input and behavior ticks.
line2: Choose it for a deliberately silent layer; Keys and Sequencer provide manual grid playing.

title: Keys
line1: Turns the grid into a direct playable key surface.
line2: Good for hands-on notes and real-time input instead of autonomous rules.

title: Sequencer
line1: A plain 8x8 step grid; press a tile to switch it on or off.
line2: It never changes by itself, so Link plays exactly what you drew.

title: Looper
line1: Captures and repeats played gestures on the layer.
line2: Nudge it live to build loops that still belong to the grid world.

title: Weave
line1: Interlaces repeating strands into a woven pattern.
line2: Useful for braided motion where simple parts keep crossing in musical ways.

title: Polyrhythm
line1: Layers pulse cycles with different lengths.
line2: Use it for rhythms that phase against each other without losing the beat.

title: Breaks
line1: Generates chopped rhythmic break patterns.
line2: Good for busier percussion worlds with gaps, kicks, and sudden turns.

title: Fills
line1: Adds fill-like bursts around the base rhythm.
line2: Use it to make transitions and accents without drawing every hit by hand.

title: Clave
line1: Builds rhythm around clave-style anchor patterns.
line2: A sturdy syncopated spine for other layers to orbit.

title: Groove
line1: Creates timing patterns with a looser pocket.
line2: Use it when the layer should lean, answer, and leave a little air.

title: Euclid
line1: Spreads hits evenly across a cycle.
line2: Great for compact rhythms that feel intentional at many lengths.

title: Ostinato
line1: Repeats a short musical figure with variation.
line2: Use it as a persistent hook for other worlds to push against.

title: Motif
line1: Develops small melodic cells into phrases.
line2: Good for recognizable ideas that can still wander.

title: Canon
line1: Moves a melodic lane across the grid with delayed voices on later rows.
line2: Density and variation add neighboring echoes; Cycle controls the phrase length.

title: Chords
line1: Builds stacked pitch rows from a moving root, then adds interval rows as density rises.
line2: Variation changes the upper interval choice; Cycle controls how often the chord pattern shifts.

title: Contour
line1: Shapes pitch motion around rising and falling curves.
line2: Use it when the melody's outline matters more than any one note.

title: Cadence
line1: Leans phrases toward arrival and release points.
line2: Good for making algorithmic layers feel like they breathe in sections.

title: Phrase
line1: Builds longer musical gestures from smaller choices.
line2: Use it for a layer that should speak in sentences, not ticks.

title: Life
line1: Runs Conway-style cellular life on the grid.
line2: Tiny seeds can settle, explode, or blink into musical events.

title: Brain
line1: Uses three-state cellular rules with firing and recovery.
line2: Good for waves of activity that leave afterimages behind.

title: Cyclic
line1: Cells advance to the next state when enough nearby cells already have that state.
line2: States sets the cycle count; Threshold and Range control how readily fronts advance.

title: Forest Fire
line1: Lets growth and ignition compete across the grid.
line2: Sparse sparks can become crackling bursts and then empty space again.

title: Predator Prey
line1: Runs chasing populations that feed and fade.
line2: Good for unstable musical ecosystems with pursuit and collapse.

title: Twinkle
line1: A sparse little sky of short-lived stars.
line2: Blue-white tiles come and go, a lovely restless layer.

title: Ant
line1: Walks rule-driven agents across cell trails.
line2: Simple turns can carve surprisingly organized paths.

title: Boids
line1: A flock of birds that keep apart, line up and stick together.
line2: Scatter Flock sends them off; Seed Flock gathers them in the middle.

title: Physarum
line1: Slime mold that follows its own trails and food; the trails fade over time.
line2: Relocate Food moves the food; Seed Slime gathers the slime again.

title: Bounce
line1: Sends motion bouncing around boundaries.
line2: A lively choice for ricochets, repeats, and kinetic accents.

title: Bubbles
line1: Lets soft moving blobs rise and overlap.
line2: Use it for buoyant motion with rounded, drifting events.

title: Coral
line1: Grows two competing cardinal-neighbor colonies, turning contested tiles into aging skeleton.
line2: Seed Coral restores the two lower-edge colonies; Break Coral removes old skeleton and exposed tiles.

title: Cracks
line1: Builds stress in clear pane tiles, advances crack tips, and branches until a bounded shatter clears it.
line2: Impact creates a center tip and stress burst; Replace Pane clears cracks and stress.

title: Crystal Growth
line1: Builds faceted growth from ordered rules.
line2: Good for patterns that feel mineral, angular, and accumulative.

title: DLA
line1: Aggregates wandering particles into branching clusters.
line2: Use it when you want chance walks to freeze into structure.

title: Ink
line1: Stores pigment strength per tile, diffuses it toward neighbors, and fades it each tick.
line2: Drop Ink adds a center splash; Clear Ink removes all pigment; scheduled drops use Drop Interval.

title: Ising
line1: Little magnets that want to agree with their neighbors, unless heat and noise shake them.
line2: Heat Pulse adds one hot step; Flip Field turns the pull around.

title: Kuramoto
line1: Synchronizes oscillators across the grid.
line2: Good for phase-locking motion that can drift into collective pulses.

title: Lightning
line1: Advances leaders toward a selected edge, branches them, then turns the connected strike into a decaying flash.
line2: Branch, Jitter, Decay, and Leader Limit shape the strike; Strike Now starts it over.

title: Wave
line1: Simulates displacement and velocity on every tile; tension spreads an impulse and damping removes energy.
line2: Grid press or Drop Impulse hits a tile; Impulse Interval adds scheduled hits.

title: Raindrops
line1: Drops impacts that ripple outward.
line2: Use it for scattered events that bloom into circles.

title: Reaction Diffusion
line1: Evolves chemical-like patterns in a field.
line2: Good for spots, stripes, and slow transformations.

title: Rivers
line1: Moves flow through channels across the grid.
line2: Use it for current, branching streams, and directional drift.

title: Gravity
line1: Sand that falls toward an edge and slides off piles.
line2: Drop Sand pours more; Clear Bottom empties the floor; Invert Gravity turns it.

title: Orbit
line1: Moves particles with attractor pull and tangential steering; particles and attractor reflect at grid edges.
line2: Reset Orbit restores a centered ring; Nudge Attractor changes its velocity for later ticks.

title: Lava Lamp
line1: Moves blobs in slow merging currents.
line2: Good for warm, drifting motion that never quite repeats.

title: Sand Ripples
line1: Forms granular ripples and shifting ridges.
line2: Use it for textured motion that rolls through the field.

title: Fractal Explorer
line1: Flies slowly through the Mandelbrot or Julia set.
line2: Jump Region flies elsewhere; Toggle Fractal Mode switches sets.

title: Maze Growth
line1: Carves maze-like paths as it expands.
line2: Use it for corridors, turns, and branching travel.

title: Shapes
line1: Creates geometric figures and spatial motifs.
line2: Good for crisp forms that other layers can answer.

title: Vines
line1: Grows tendrils that curl and branch.
line2: Use it for reaching lines and organic melodic creep.

title: Back
line1: Returns to the parent browser level.
line2: Use it like the hardware Back button when browsing synthetic folders.

title: Bind Parameter
line1: Puts this setting on the control you are picking for.
line2: A setting another control already owns cannot be taken; you get a toast.

title: Behavior Params
line1: Targets from the selected layer's behavior settings.
line2: Choose these to let modulation steer the active world-bubble itself.

title: Link
line1: Tempo and Link settings.
line2: Bind these for tempo-aware moves.

title: Shape Targets
line1: Instrument, mixer, FX, and voice-shaping targets.
line2: This is where modulation reaches the sound-making machinery.

title: Instruments
line1: Targets from individual instrument slots.
line2: Pick a slot, then bind synth, sample, MIDI, mixer, or routing parameters.

title: Play FX
line1: Targets from live performance FX pages.
line2: Bind these when aux or grid gestures should push performance effects.

title: System Targets
line1: Global sound settings that are safe to modulate.
line2: These apply outside a single behavior or instrument slot.

title: Sound
line1: Note length, velocity scale and polyphony.
line2: Handy for performance controls over all notes.

title: (none)
line1: Clears this control, so it moves nothing.

title: MIDI Active
line1: Switches all MIDI in and out on or off.
line2: Pick the ports under MIDI Host.

title: Send MIDI
line1: MIDI inst. sends only MIDI Inst. and MIDI Drum notes; all inst. also sends Synth, FM, Plucked, Drum and Sampler notes.
line2: Internal notes go out on their slot's channel, 1 to 8. Drum hits use GM notes, Sampler slots 36 to 43, 100 ms each. Muted slots send nothing.

title: Sync Mode
line1: internal uses Octessera's transport clock; external follows incoming MIDI clock when Clock In is enabled.
line2: The selected source controls transport timing; Clock Out independently sends MIDI clock.

title: State Notes
line1: Plays lit tiles on every step, not only when they change.
line2: Turn it off to hear only changes.

title: Curve
line1: linear spreads values evenly; curve starts slow and rises late.
line2: From and To stay the ends either way.

title: Curve
line1: linear spreads values evenly; curve starts slow and rises late.
line2: From and To stay the ends either way.

title: X Lane From
line1: Sets the low endpoint for this X-axis value lane.
line2: The lane scales grid position between From and To.

title: X Lane To
line1: Sets the high endpoint for this X-axis value lane.
line2: The lane scales grid position between From and To.

title: X Grid Offset
line1: Rotates the X-axis lane index before scaling values.
line2: Useful for shifting where low and high modulation points fall on the grid.

title: Y Lane From
line1: Sets the low endpoint for this Y-axis value lane.
line2: The lane scales grid position between From and To.

title: Y Lane To
line1: Sets the high endpoint for this Y-axis value lane.
line2: The lane scales grid position between From and To.

title: Y Grid Offset
line1: Rotates the Y-axis lane index before scaling values.
line2: Useful for shifting where low and high modulation points fall on the grid.

title: Sampler
line1: Configures sample-slot playback, grid assignment, velocity levels, filter, and amp shaping.
line2: Visible for sampler instruments.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Sampler > Velocity Levels
title: Velocity Levels
line1: Configures High, Medium, and Low velocities for assigned sampler tiles.
line2: Visible when Velocity Levels is on.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Sampler > Amp Env
title: Amp Envelope
line1: Shapes sampler loudness over time with ADSR stages.
line2: Attack/Decay/Release are milliseconds; Sustain is percentage.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Sampler > Filter Env
title: Filter Envelope
line1: Shapes sampler filter motion over time with ADSR stages.
line2: Use with filter Env Amount for plucks and sweeps.

title: Tune Semis
line1: Transposes sampler playback in semitones.
line2: Negative values tune down; positive values tune up.

title: Tile Tune
line1: Semitone offset that Assign stamps onto each tile you press.
line2: Stamped per tile; changing it later only affects tiles you stamp again.

title: Tile Fine
line1: Cent offset that Assign stamps onto each tile you press.
line2: Stamped per tile; combine with Tile Tune for microtonal or chromatic layouts.

title: Tile Level
line1: Velocity tier Assign stamps onto each tile: Base, High, Medium or Low velocity.
line2: High/Medium/Low play the Vel Levels velocities; Base uses the normal velocity.

title: Follow Transpose
line1: When on, Play Transpose also shifts this sampler's assigned tiles.
line2: Off keeps sampled tiles at their stamped pitch whatever the transpose.

title: Follow Pitch
line1: When on, tiles play the Link note, with C4 at the stamped pitch.
line2: Stamp Tile Tune/Fine so each sample sounds right at C4; off plays stamped pitch only.

title: Follow Pitch
line1: When on, drum tiles play the Link note, with C4 at the stamped pitch.
line2: Off keeps each tile at its stamped pitch whatever note Link sends.

title: Follow Transpose
line1: When on, Play Transpose also shifts this drum kit's assigned tiles.
line2: Off keeps drum tiles at their stamped pitch whatever the transpose.

title: Level High
line1: Velocity played by drum tiles stamped with Tile Level High.
line2: Final velocity is still scaled by Link/global velocity shaping.

title: Level Medium
line1: Velocity played by drum tiles stamped with Tile Level Medium.
line2: Final velocity is still scaled by Link/global velocity shaping.

title: Level Low
line1: Velocity played by drum tiles stamped with Tile Level Low.
line2: Final velocity is still scaled by Link/global velocity shaping.

title: Sample Gain
line1: Sets base sampler loudness for this instrument slot.
line2: Use with mixer volume and master volume for level balance.

title: Sample Velocity Sensitivity
line1: Controls how strongly trigger velocity affects sampler loudness.
line2: Lower values flatten dynamics; higher values increase response.

title: Sample Filter Type
line1: lowpass keeps lows; highpass keeps highs; bandpass keeps a band; notch removes a band around cutoff.
line2: Cutoff, resonance, and Filter Env shape the selected sampler response.

title: Sample Filter Cutoff
line1: Sets the sampler filter cutoff; 0..255 spans 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
line2: Samples start fully open (top, Res 0), which skips the filter; a highpass at 0 is open too.

title: Sample Filter Resonance
line1: Boosts emphasis near the sampler filter cutoff.
line2: High values create stronger peaks.

title: Sample Filter Env Amount
line1: Sets how much the sampler filter envelope moves cutoff.
line2: Positive values open with envelope; negative values invert.

title: Sample Filter Key Tracking
line1: Sets how sampler filter cutoff follows played pitch.
line2: Higher values keep timbre more consistent across pitch.

title: Type
line1: None is silent; Synth plays oscillators; Sampler plays samples; FM bends sine tones; Plucked rings strings; Drum makes hits.
line2: MIDI Inst. sends notes to MIDI gear; MIDI Drum sends its stamped tiles as MIDI drum notes. Only the rows of the chosen type show.

title: MIDI Velocity
line1: Sets fixed outgoing note velocity for this MIDI instrument slot.
line2: Use when Link should drive pitch/timing but not velocity dynamics.

title: MIDI Duration
line1: Sets default outgoing MIDI note length in milliseconds.
line2: Useful for shaping external MIDI staccato or sustain.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > MIDI Drum
title: MIDI Drum
line1: Turns Link hits on stamped tiles into MIDI notes for external drum gear.
line2: It sends MIDI only, never sound or audio FX. Unstamped tiles stay silent.

title: MIDI Drum Enabled
line1: Turns this MIDI Drum's note output on or off.
line2: System > MIDI > MIDI Active and a MIDI output must be on too. Mix mute silences it.

title: MIDI Drum Channel
line1: The MIDI channel its notes go out on, 1 to 16.
line2: Channel 10 is where General MIDI gear keeps its drums.

title: MIDI Drum Duration
line1: How long each note holds before its note-off, 10 to 2000 ms.
line2: Most one-shot drum sounds ignore it; gated or looped sounds follow it.

title: Note
line1: The note Assign stamps onto each tile you press, 0 to 127.
line2: Shown with its note name (middle C is C4) and General MIDI drum name, like 36 C2 Kick.

title: Tile Vel
line1: The velocity Assign stamps onto each tile you press, 1 to 127.
line2: A stamped tile always sends its own velocity, whatever Link plays.

title: Assign MIDI Drum Tiles
line1: Stamps Note and Tile Vel onto each grid tile you press.
line2: Pressing an exact match clears it; Shift does a row (bottom is y=0), Shift+Fn a column. Back leaves.

title: Synth
line1: Configures the internal two-oscillator synth for this slot.
line2: Visible for synth instruments.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Synth > Amp Env
title: Amp Envelope
line1: Shapes synth loudness over time with ADSR stages.
line2: Attack/Decay/Release are milliseconds; Sustain is percentage.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Synth > Filter Env
title: Filter Envelope
line1: Shapes synth filter motion over time with ADSR stages.
line2: Use with filter Env Amount for plucks and sweeps.

title: FM
line1: Shapes a sine carrier with a sine modulator for this slot.
line2: Preset loads a starting sound; Tone, Index Env, Filter, Volume, Amp Env, and Filter Env shape it.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > FM > Tone
title: Tone
line1: Ratio and Fine set modulator pitch against the carrier; Index controls modulation depth.
line2: Tone edits can reshape a note already ringing.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > FM > Index Env
title: Index Envelope
line1: Shapes FM modulation depth with its own ADSR, separate from loudness and filter movement.
line2: Attack/Decay/Release are in ms; Sustain is a percentage.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > FM > Filter
title: Filter
line1: Shapes this FM voice after the two-operator tone is made.
line2: Type, cutoff, resonance, envelope amount, and key tracking work like Synth.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > FM > Volume
title: Volume
line1: Sets FM voice gain and its velocity response.
line2: The separate Mixer volume and route set the slot's place in the full mix.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > FM > Amp Env
title: Amp Envelope
line1: Shapes FM loudness over time with ADSR stages.
line2: Attack/Decay/Release are in ms; Sustain is a percentage.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > FM > Filter Env
title: Filter Envelope
line1: Shapes FM filter movement over time with ADSR stages.
line2: Use with filter Env Amount to open or close the tone.

title: FM Ratio
line1: 0.5 (1:2) places the modulator below the carrier; 1 (1:1) matches it; 2 (2:1), 3 (3:1), and 4 (4:1) climb higher.
line2: 5 (5:1), 6 (6:1), and 8 (8:1) add brighter harmonics. Stored as exact ratio strings.

title: Fine
line1: Offsets the modulator relative to the carrier by -100 to +100 cents.
line2: This tunes the modulator interval, not the carrier's pitch.

title: FM Index
line1: Sets modulation depth from 0 to 100; 50 means 2 radians, and 100 means 4 radians.
line2: Index Env shapes this depth independently of the Amp and Filter envelopes.

title: Vel to Index
line1: Sets how much note velocity scales Index from 0 to 100%.
line2: Changes harmonic depth rather than directly scaling amplitude or Volume.

title: Mod Shape
line1: Blends in a second harmonic of the modulator from 0 to 100%.
line2: Only adds shape when Index is above 0.

title: Mod Mix
line1: Adds an audible modulator tone from 0 to 100%, even when Index is 0.
line2: At Ratio 1, the modulator can reinforce the carrier.

title: FM Gain
line1: Sets base FM loudness from 0 to 100, starting at 80.
line2: Mixer volume and Master Vol also affect the final internal-audio level.

title: FM Velocity Sensitivity
line1: Sets how much trigger velocity changes FM loudness from 0 to 100, starting at 100.
line2: Lower values flatten the response; higher values keep more dynamics.

title: FM Filter Type
line1: lowpass keeps lows; highpass keeps highs; bandpass keeps a band; notch removes a band around cutoff.
line2: Cutoff, resonance, and Filter Env shape the selected response.

title: FM Filter Cutoff
line1: Sets base cutoff on the same 0..255 display scale as Synth.
line2: Higher values pass more high content.

title: FM Filter Resonance
line1: Boosts emphasis near the filter cutoff on the same 0..255 scale as Synth.
line2: High resonance can make sharp tonal peaks.

title: FM Filter Env Amount
line1: Sets how much the filter envelope moves cutoff, from -100 to 100.
line2: Positive values open with the envelope; negative values invert.

title: FM Filter Key Tracking
line1: Sets how cutoff follows played pitch from 0 to 100.
line2: Higher values keep timbre more consistent across pitches.

title: Plucked
line1: Sets up the string voice for this instrument slot.
line2: Preset loads a starting sound; String, Filter, Volume, Amp Env, and Filter Env shape it.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Plucked > String
title: String
line1: Decay and Brightness can reshape ringing notes; Pick Pos, Pick Depth, Stiffness, and body controls shape the next pluck.
line2: Body Freq moves body coloration when Body Amt is enabled; it is dormant at zero Body Amt.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Plucked > Filter
title: Plucked Filter
line1: Shapes the plucked voice after string excitation.
line2: Type, cutoff, resonance, envelope amount, and key tracking use Synth's control scales.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Plucked > Volume
title: Plucked Volume
line1: Sets string gain and response to trigger velocity.
line2: Mixer volume and route place the slot in the full mix.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Plucked > Amp Env
title: Plucked Amp Envelope
line1: Shapes the plucked voice's loudness with ADSR stages.
line2: Time controls are in ms; Sustain is a percentage.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Plucked > Filter Env
title: Plucked Filter Envelope
line1: Shapes filter movement with ADSR stages.
line2: Use with Filter Env Amount to shape the sound after the pick.

title: String Decay
line1: Sets string ring time from 100 to 5000 ms, starting at 1500 ms.
line2: Longer values keep the string sounding for longer.

title: String Brightness
line1: Controls string brightness from 0 to 100%, starting at 65%.
line2: Higher values retain more upper harmonics as the string rings.

title: Pick Position
line1: Sets where the next pluck excites the string, from 5 to 50%, starting at 25%.
line2: This fast next-pluck setting does not reshape a note already ringing.

title: Pick Depth
line1: Sets the next pluck's excitation depth from 0 to 100%, starting at 65%.
line2: Changes excitation color, not Pick Pos or string Brightness.

title: Stiffness
line1: Shapes the next pluck's upper partials toward wire-like inharmonicity, from 0 to 100%.
line2: This is not a literal steel, nylon, string-weight, or tension model.

title: Body Amt
line1: Adds body coloration outside the string feedback from 0 to 100%, starting at 0.
line2: Applies to the next pluck; Body Freq is dormant while Body Amt is 0.

title: Body Freq
line1: Sets the next pluck's body-coloration frequency from 100 to 2000 Hz, starting at 500 Hz.
line2: It moves body coloration when enabled; it is not the shared Filter cutoff.

title: Plucked Gain
line1: Sets base string loudness from 0 to 100%, starting at 80%.
line2: Mixer volume and Master Vol also affect the final internal-audio level.

title: Plucked Velocity Sensitivity
line1: Sets how much trigger velocity changes string loudness from 0 to 100%, starting at 100%.
line2: Lower values flatten the response; higher values keep more dynamics.

title: Plucked Filter Type
line1: lowpass keeps lows; highpass keeps highs; bandpass keeps a band; notch removes a band near cutoff.
line2: Cutoff, resonance, and Filter Env shape the selected response.

title: Plucked Filter Cutoff
line1: Sets base cutoff on Synth's 0..255 display scale.
line2: Higher values pass more high content.

title: Plucked Filter Resonance
line1: Boosts emphasis near the filter cutoff on Synth's 0..255 scale.
line2: High resonance can make sharp tonal peaks.

title: Plucked Filter Env Amount
line1: Sets how much Filter Env moves the cutoff, from -100 to 100%.
line2: Positive values open with the envelope; negative values invert it.

title: Plucked Filter Key Tracking
line1: Sets how cutoff follows pitch from 0 to 100%.
line2: Higher values keep timbre more consistent across pitches.

title: Drum
line1: Configures one eight-voice drum kit in this instrument slot.
line2: Kit loads voice settings; Voice picks a sound to edit; Assign maps it to tiles.

title: Drum Voice
line1: Selects V1: Kick, V2: Snare, V3: Closed Hat, V4: Open Hat, V5: Low Tom, V6: High Tom, V7: Clap, or V8: Rim by default.
line2: Each V1..V8 name follows its current Sound; changing Voice chooses which kit voice to edit or assign.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Drum > Edit
title: Edit Drum Voice
line1: Adjusts Sound, Tune, Decay, Tone, Attack, Sweep, Noise, and Level on the selected kit voice.
line2: Changes affect future hits using that voice, including tiles already assigned to it.

title: Sound
line1: The drum this voice plays: Kick, Snare, Closed Hat, Open Hat, Low Tom, High Tom, Clap or Rim.
line2: Changing it resets this voice's sound settings to suit the new drum.

title: Drum Voice Tune
line1: Offsets the selected kit voice from its Sound's base pitch by -12..12 semitones.
line2: Applies to future hits; individual assigned tiles may have their own extra Tile Tune.

title: Drum Voice Decay
line1: Sets the selected voice's next-hit decay from 20 to 2000 ms.
line2: The default depends on Sound; editing does not morph a hit already ringing.

title: Drum Voice Tone
line1: Sets the next hit's tone from 0 to 100%.
line2: Higher values emphasize brightness/noise and upper modes without changing a ringing hit.

title: Drum Voice Attack
line1: Sets the onset fade for the next hit from 0 to 50 ms.
line2: Short attacks make a sharper strike; it does not retarget an active hit.

title: Drum Sweep Pitch
line1: Sets next-hit pitch-sweep depth from 0 to 36 semitones.
line2: Sweep Time sets its duration; at 0 ms, the hit has no sweep excursion.

title: Drum Sweep Time
line1: Sets next-hit pitch-sweep duration from 0 to 200 ms.
line2: At 0 ms, the hit has no sweep excursion even when Sweep Pitch is above 0.

title: Drum Noise
line1: Sets the next hit's mix from pitched tone at 0% to noise at 100%.
line2: The default depends on Sound; editing does not change a hit already ringing.

title: Drum Voice Level
line1: Attenuates the selected kit voice's next hit from 0 to 100%.
line2: This is per-voice level, not the kit-wide Gain in Volume.

title: Assign Drum Tiles
line1: Stamps the selected kit voice plus the Tile rows onto each grid tile you press.
line2: Pressing an exact match clears it; Shift does a row (bottom is y=0), the combined modifier a column.

title: Preview Drum Voice
line1: Main press plays one hit from the selected voice at its own Tune, without a tile offset.
line2: This is not Space or a sample-browser preview; it emits an internal Drum hit.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Drum > Filter
title: Drum Filter
line1: Shapes this slot's drum voices through the shared filter.
line2: Type, cutoff, resonance, envelope amount, and key tracking use Synth's control scales.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Drum > Vel Levels
title: Drum Vel Levels
line1: Velocities that drum tiles stamped with Tile Level High, Medium or Low play.
line2: Base tiles keep the trigger velocity; each kit slot has its own three levels.

path: Menu > Shape > Instruments > Instrument * > Drum > Volume
title: Drum Volume
line1: Sets kit-wide gain and trigger-velocity response.
line2: Mixer volume and route place this internal audio slot in the full mix.

title: Drum Filter Type
line1: lowpass keeps lows; highpass keeps highs; bandpass keeps a band; notch removes a band near cutoff.
line2: Changing Type prepares the slot; use Cutoff and Res for live shaping.

title: Drum Filter Cutoff
line1: Sets kit-wide cutoff on Synth's 0..255 display scale.
line2: Higher values pass more high content while hits play.

title: Drum Filter Resonance
line1: Sets emphasis near the kit-wide filter cutoff on Synth's 0..255 scale.
line2: Higher values can make sharp peaks while hits play.

title: Drum Filter Env Amount
line1: Sets filter-envelope motion from -100 to 100% for future hits.
line2: Positive values open the filter; negative values invert the contour.

title: Drum Filter Key Tracking
line1: Sets cutoff tracking with pitch from 0 to 100% for future hits.
line2: Higher values keep timbre steadier across tuned hits.

title: Drum Gain
line1: Sets kit-wide gain from 0 to 100%, starting at 80%.
line2: Mixer volume and Master Vol still set the final level.

title: Drum Vel Sens
line1: Sets how strongly trigger velocity changes drum loudness from 0 to 100%, starting at 100%.
line2: This setting applies to future hits.

title: Target
line1: What the Play FX processes: master (the whole mix), fxb1, fxb2, fxb3 or fxb4 (one FX bus),
line2: or I1, I2, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 or I8 (one instrument); MIDI instruments make no sound here.

title: XY Axis
line1: The setting this axis of the XY pad moves.
line2: A setting another control already owns cannot be taken; you get a toast.

title: Behavior Parameters
line1: Lists behavior parameters available for binding.
line2: Selecting a row binds that parameter to the current target slot.

title: Instrument Parameters
line1: Lists instrument parameters available for binding.
line2: Selecting a row binds that parameter to the current target slot.

title: Instrument
line1: The settings of this instrument you can pick.
line2: Only the current type's settings have an effect.

title: Sampler
line1: The sampler settings you can pick.

title: Synth
line1: The synth settings you can pick.

title: Drum
line1: The settings of the selected drum voice and the whole kit you can pick.
line2: Tune, Decay, Tone and Attack change the next hit, not one already ringing.

title: Drum Voice Targets
line1: Bind Tune, Decay, Tone, or Attack for the selected kit voice.
line2: The saved binding names its voice number; edits affect later hits.

title: Drum Filter Targets
line1: Bind this slot's audible Cutoff or Res controls.
line2: Filter Type is a structural menu choice, not a smooth numeric target.

title: Drum Volume Target
line1: Bind kit-wide Gain before the slot's Mixer volume.
line2: The value changes audio without replacing a voice or kit assignment.

title: Plucked
line1: The Plucked settings you can pick.
line2: Pick Pos changes the next pluck, not one already ringing.

title: Sound Parameters
line1: Lists global sound parameters available for binding.
line2: Selecting a row binds that parameter to the current target slot.

title: Range Min
line1: The lowest value this control may set.
line2: Use Min and Max to keep a control in a sweet spot.

title: Range Max
line1: Sets the high end of the current numeric binding's user range.
line2: Set equal to Range Min for a fixed modulation value.

title: Link Delay
line1: Delays this Link event target by layer link ticks.
line2: 0 is immediate; delayed events use the already-routed event and do not re-roll probability.

title: Link Retrig
line1: Adds extra repeats after this Link event target.
line2: A value of 2 repeats at delay+1 and delay+2 layer ticks.

title: Duck Amount
line1: Sets how strongly ducking reduces the target bus (0–100%).
line2: Higher percentages create deeper ducking.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Slot *: * > Attack
title: Attack
line1: Sets how quickly this effect reacts after input crosses its trigger condition.
line2: Short values respond faster.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Slot *: Duck > Attack
title: Attack
line1: Sets Duck attack time; accepted values are 1–500 ms.
line2: Short values respond faster.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Slot *: * > Release
title: Release
line1: Sets how quickly this effect returns after release or input falls away.
line2: Longer values decay more slowly.

path: Menu > Shape > FX Buses > B*: * > Slot *: Duck > Release
title: Release
line1: Sets Duck release time; accepted values are 1–5000 ms.
line2: Longer values decay more slowly.

title: Threshold
line1: Sets the normalized trigger level for this effect from 0 to 1.
line2: Lower values trigger more easily.

title: Threshold dB
line1: Sets compressor threshold in dB.
line2: Signals above this level are reduced.

title: Mix
line1: Sets wet/dry mix for this effect.
line2: 0 is dry; 100 is fully wet.

title: Time Mode
line1: ms sets a fixed delay time; note follows the tempo.
line2: Only the matching time row shows.

title: Time Note
line2: 1/2T, 1/2, 1/1T or 1/1 (T means triplet). It follows the tempo.

title: Delay Time
line1: Sets delay time in milliseconds; shown in ms mode.
line2: Longer values create wider echoes.

title: Delay Spread
line1: Widens Delay at the FX bus output.
line2: 0% keeps the current mono bus output; Mix 0 produces no spread.

title: Feedback
line1: Sets how much output feeds back into the effect.
line2: Higher values increase repeats or resonance.

title: Rate
line1: Sets modulation rate in Hertz.
line2: Higher rates move faster.

title: Depth
line1: Sets modulation depth as a percentage.
line2: Higher values create stronger movement.

title: Depth
line1: Sets modulation depth in milliseconds.
line2: Used by chorus, flanger, and vibrato style effects.

title: Base
line1: Sets the base delay time in milliseconds.
line2: Depth is applied around this base.

title: Drive
line1: Sets nonlinear drive amount.
line2: Higher values add more saturation or distortion.

title: Clip
line1: Sets distortion clipping threshold.
line2: Lower values clip harder.

title: Bits
line1: Sets bit depth for bitcrushing.
line2: Lower values sound rougher.

title: Rate Div
line1: Sets sample-rate reduction divisor.
line2: Higher values reduce more aggressively.

title: Center Hz
line1: Sets the center frequency for filter modulation.
line2: This anchors the sweep range.

title: Q
line1: Sets filter resonance/Q.
line2: Higher values emphasize the cutoff region.

title: Decay
line1: Sets reverb feedback decay.
line2: Displayed as approximate tail time.

title: Damp
line1: Sets reverb high-frequency damping.
line2: Higher values darken the tail faster.

title: Chance
line1: Sets glitch trigger probability.
line2: Higher values glitch more often.

title: Slice
line1: Sets glitch slice length.
line2: Shorter slices sound tighter and more fragmented.

title: Ratio
line1: Sets compressor ratio.
line2: Higher ratios reduce peaks more strongly.

title: Makeup
line1: Adds gain after compression.
line2: Use it to recover level after gain reduction.

title: Low Gain
line1: Adjusts low-band EQ gain.
line2: Negative cuts lows; positive boosts lows.

title: Mid Gain
line1: Adjusts mid-band EQ gain.
line2: Negative cuts mids; positive boosts mids.

title: High Gain
line1: Adjusts high-band EQ gain.
line2: Negative cuts highs; positive boosts highs.

title: Mid Frequency
line1: Sets the EQ mid-band center frequency.
line2: Move it to target different tonal ranges.

title: Mid Q
line1: Sets the EQ mid-band width.
line2: Higher values make a narrower band.

title: Saturation

path: Menu > Play > FX > Map to Grid
title: Map to Grid
line1: Enters FX assignment mode using the current effect type and values.
line2: Press a grid tile to store it; Back exits assignment mode.

title: X Axis
line1: Selects which parameter the X axis modulates. Options include the same mappable parameters available for aux encoders and X/Y Link modulation.
line2: Choose (none) to disable X axis modulation.

title: Y Axis
line1: Selects which parameter the Y axis modulates. Options include the same mappable parameters available for aux encoders and X/Y Link modulation.
line2: Choose (none) to disable Y axis modulation.

title: Glide
line1: Controls the glide time for mapped X/Y values, up to 5 seconds.
line2: Off jumps immediately; longer values glide slower. The raw grid marker remains immediate.

title: Release Behavior
line1: sample-hold keeps the last X/Y modulation value; reset-center returns both axes to center (0.5, 0.5).
line2: This choice applies when the Play XY grid touch is released, unless Shift + press latched it.

title: Invert X
line1: Flips the X axis value.
line2: When on, left becomes maximum and right becomes minimum.

title: Invert Y
line1: Flips the Y axis value.
line2: When on, bottom becomes maximum and top becomes minimum.

title: Seed
line1: The shared seed for every layer and Link section you've switched to Seeded.
line2: Reload the patch with the same seed and play it the same way for the same surprises; change it to reroll them all.

title: Seeded
line1: When On, this layer's behavior draws its randomness from the Build Seed.
line2: Its dice restart on play-from-stop and patch load, but an evolved world keeps its tiles; reload or Reset to replay. Off keeps it freshly random.

title: Seeded
line1: When On, this layer's trigger probability and random arp order follow the Build Seed.
line2: Off keeps them on the shared unseeded stream, as before.

title: Fire Threshold
line1: How many firing neighbors wake a resting cell.
line2: 2 is the classic Brian's Brain; 1 spreads wildly, 3 and 4 calm it down.

title: Spawn Count
line1: How many cells Seed Brain and Seed Interval light up.
line2: Off seeds nothing.

title: Max Ants
line1: The most ants that walk at once.
line2: Spawn Ant and Spawn Interval stop adding ants at this count.

title: Spawn Interval
line1: Adds an ant every this many steps.
line2: Off adds ants only when you ask.

title: Max Balls
line1: The most balls that bounce at once.
line2: New balls wait until there is room.

title: Lifespan
line1: How many steps a shape grows before it fades.
line2: Longer lifespans draw bigger shapes.

title: Spawn Interval
line1: Starts a new shape every this many steps.
line2: Off starts shapes only when you press the grid.

title: Splash Radius
line1: How far a raindrop's ripple travels.
line2: Off keeps splashes to the tile they land on.

title: X Slot
line1: Picks a setting that follows a tile's left-right position.
line2: Pick (none) to clear it.

title: Y Slot
line1: Picks a setting that follows a tile's bottom-top position.
line2: Pick (none) to clear it.

title: Arp
line1: Turns this layer's notes into arpeggios.
line2: Pick a Mode, then shape it with Step, Length and Gate.

title: Filter Cutoff
line1: This layer's X and Y filter cutoff lanes.

title: Filter Res
line1: This layer's X and Y filter resonance lanes.

title: Velocity
line1: This layer's X and Y velocity lanes.

title: Play FX
line1: The settings of the momentary Play FX.

title: Pan Pos: from bus
line1: This instrument plays through an FX bus, so the bus's Pan Pos places it.
line2: Set Route to direct to pan it here.

title: Empty Slot
line1: An empty effect slot.
line2: Open it and pick a Type to add an effect.

title: Delay
line1: Echoes, either in milliseconds or in time with the tempo.
line2: Feedback sets how many repeats; Spread widens them.

title: Reverb
line1: A room around the sound.
line2: Decay sets its size, Damp darkens the tail.

title: Duck
line1: Turns this bus down while another instrument or bus plays.
line2: The classic pumping sidechain trick.

title: Tremolo
line1: Wobbles the volume.
line2: Rate sets the speed, Depth how deep.

title: Saturator
line1: Gentle warmth and grit.
line2: Drive pushes it harder.

title: Distortion
line1: Hard clipping crunch.
line2: Drive and Clip set how nasty.

title: Bitcrusher
line1: Lo-fi digital grit.
line2: Fewer Bits and a higher Rate Div crush harder.

title: Vibrato
line1: Wobbles the pitch.
line2: Rate sets the speed, Depth how far.

title: Chorus
line1: Thickens the sound with slightly detuned copies.

title: Flanger
line1: A swooshing jet sweep.
line2: Feedback makes it ring.

title: Filter LFO
line1: A filter that sweeps up and down by itself.
line2: Center sets where, Depth how far.

title: Wah
line1: A vocal wah-wah sweep.

title: Auto Pan
line1: Swings the sound from left to right.

title: Glitch
line1: Randomly repeats short slices.
line2: Chance sets how often.

title: Compressor
line1: Evens out loud and quiet parts.
line2: Threshold and Ratio set how hard it squeezes.

title: EQ
line1: Three-band tone control.
line2: Boost or cut lows, mids and highs.

title: Vinyl
line1: Old record charm: warmth, crackle and wobble.
